title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from 2.1–2.4 on the previous pages). X is smooth projective of dimension n over k. Y is an auxiliary smooth projective curve, for instance a general complete-intersection curve, as the next page makes explicit. A divisorial correspondence Z between Y and X induces two maps:
- a cohomological map H^1(Y) -> H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1);
- an 'arithmetic' map u on abelian varieties: Albanese/Picard type morphisms B_X -> A_Y and so on.
Prop. 2.4 (end of p.63) says the cohomological map is invertible on T_l iff u is an isogeny. The inverse then exists in Hom_Q and is again given by a Q-cycle whose best denominator is controlled by an integer N, essentially the degree of the isogeny. For l = p, the previous page indicates the same works through isocrystals.

Corollary 2.5 is the integral refinement. For l != char k, N is prime to l iff the composite H^1(Y,Z_l) -> H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)(n-1) -> H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)(n-1)/torsion is bijective. For H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l) to be torsion-free as well, it suffices that H^1(Y,Z_l) -> H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)(n-1) itself be bijective.

Corollary 2.6 is hard Lefschetz in degree 1 with algebraic inverse. Let X be smooth projective connected of dimension n >= 2, and xi_1, ..., xi_{n-1} classes in Pic(X) of ample sheaves, with eta = xi_1...xi_{n-1}.
- Cup product with eta, H^1(X,Q_l) -> H^{2n-1}(X,Q_l)(n-1), is an isomorphism for every l.
- Its inverse is induced by an element of A^1(X x X) ⊗ Q, even of Cl(X,X) ⊗ Q (divisorial correspondences). The degree count is consistent: a codimension-k correspondence shifts degree by 2k-2n, and k = 1 gives 2n-1 -> 1.
- This element is unique and independent of l.

The margin note 'Th?' calls this an important special case of a 'vector Lefschetz' statement that yields the Lefschetz conjecture for surfaces. This is the degree-1 case of the Lefschetz standard conjecture B.

Proof plan, begun at the bottom and continued on p.65:
- Show that the corresponding homomorphism u: B_X -> A_X (Albanese to Picard, with A_X ≅ B_X^*) is an isogeny, better still a polarization.
- Factor u as B_X -> B_Y -> A_Y -> A_X through a general complete-intersection curve Y, where restriction and its transpose are isogenies.
- Then apply 2.4–2.5.
errors: 'pour tout entier l' should read 'for every prime l'; the l = char k case needs crystalline/isocrystal cohomology, as the previous page hints, and is not covered by Z_l-étale cohomology.
Cor. 2.5 is stated loosely: the l-torsion-freeness criterion is only a sufficient condition, and the role of N (degree of the isogeny vs. denominator of the inverse correspondence) is left implicit.

The claim that the inverse correspondence is unique should be read as uniqueness of its action on H^1 (or modulo homologically trivial correspondences), not uniqueness as a cycle class in A^1(X x X) ⊗ Q.

ideas.what: Hard Lefschetz H^1 -> H^{2n-1} with inverse given by an algebraic divisorial correspondence, independent of l; Lefschetz standard conjecture B in degree 1, hence B for surfaces
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture in degree <= 1 (via Albanese/Picard and polarization)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Standard conjectures, 1968/69); Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968), which proves B for surfaces and in degree 1
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968, publ. 1969), where B is stated as known for dim <= 2; details in Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Reduction to showing that Alb_X -> Pic^0_X induced by eta is an isogeny (a polarization), by factoring through a complete-intersection curve
ideas.modern_name: Polarization of the Albanese induced by an ample class; Lefschetz hyperplane theorem for Albanese
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Weil, Lang, Matsusaka); standard in Kleiman 1968

ideas.what: Integral (Z_l) version: l-integrality of the inverse Lefschetz correspondence is tied to l not dividing the isogeny degree N, with a criterion for torsion-freeness of H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)
ideas.modern_name: Integral Lefschetz in degree 1 / denominators of Lefschetz inverse
ideas.usually_credited_to: Not standardly singled out; folklore via the degree of the polarization

ideas.what: Uniform treatment including l = p via isocrystals / Dieudonné theory of the abelian varieties
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz in degree 1 for crystalline cohomology via Dieudonné modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Katz–Messing (1974) for crystalline compatibility

missed.claim: Grothendieck sketches an integral version of the degree-1 Lefschetz standard conjecture. The best denominator of the inverse correspondence is governed by the isogeny degree N, and l prime to N is characterized by Z_l-bijectivity modulo torsion. This integral refinement was never developed in his published texts.
missed.quote: que N soit premier à ℓ (si ℓ ≠ car k) et f. et s. que le composé H^1(Y,Z_ℓ) → H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1) → H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1)/tors soit bijectif
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and torsion versions of the standard conjectures have drawn recent interest (integral Hodge/Tate failures, torsion in Lefschetz). The content here is close to folklore, however.

deep.surprise_reason: The main content (Lefschetz B in degree 1 via Albanese/Picard polarization) is well known and was stated by Grothendieck and proved by Kleiman. Only the integral-denominator refinement and the uniform l = p treatment are mildly notable unpublished details.
transcription_corrections: 'f. et s.' abbreviates 'il faut et il suffit'.
The underlined target in the first display should read H^{2n-1}(X,Z_l)(n-1) modulo torsion (the underline marks the quotient by torsion).
In 2.6, 'pour tout entier ℓ' is likely 'pour tout premier ℓ' (handwriting ambiguous).
The margin reads roughly: 'Th? C'est un cas particulier important des "Lefschetz vectoriels" donnant "Lefschetz" pour les surfaces...'
